To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the absence of cofactors in E1 from E. coli PDHc causes the enzyme to assume a conformation that is different in several ways from the conformation adopted by the holoenzyme, but that is similar to that of the holoenzyme in the region of the ThDP cofactors.

a water molecule is found in the active site of the apo-E1 component from the alpha(2) E. coli PDHc and this water molecule forms a hydrogen-bonding network similar to that found with the thiamine pyrimidine ring in holo-E1 and PDHc E2-ThTDP-Mn(2+).
the absence of the ThDP cofactors results in a change in the hydrogen-bonding network of the active-site of PDHc E. 1, which is different to the heterotetramer branched-chain apo E1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular basis of cofactor recognition and the role of the active-site loops that undergo conformational changes in the E1 component from E. coli PDHc.
the structural and functional characterization of the pyruvic acid decarboxylation reaction catalyzed by E1 components of PDHcs.
the structural changes that take place in the active site of PDHc E2-ThDP-Mg (2+) when the enzyme is complexed with ThTDP and with the structural changes observed in the apo-enzyme.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the apo-PDHc-E1 is structurally very close to the holo-PDHc-E(1)-ThDP-Mg(II) enzyme, and is more similar to the latter than it is to the heterotetramer apo-E1-ThDP-Mn(II) complex.
the E. coli apo-E1 enzyme is not a static entity, but rather is dynamic in nature.

the absence of cofactors in PDHc E 1 apoenzymes does not cause disorder-to-order transformations of any active-site loops and that the apoenzyme structures are essentially the same as the holo-enzyme structures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the E1 apoenzye is not a good model for either the holoenzyme or the inhibitor complex, and that the E1-ThDP enzyme is the best model of E1 function.

, in the absence of cofactors, a water molecule is bound in the active site and a histidine side chain is partially disordered, whereas, in the presence of the cofactor ThDP or ThTDP, both the water and the histidine are displaced by ThDP and ThTDP, respectively.

the absence of the cofactor ThDP in apo-PDH E1 causes a rearrangement of hydrogen bonds that are normally present in the holo-E enzyme and that this rearrangement is different from that found in the heterotetameric branched-chain E1 apoenzme.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the absence of ThDP and Mg(2+), and the resulting lack of a ThDP cofactor-derived pyrimidine ring in the active site, has significant structural consequences in the homodimers alpha(2) PDHc E2, but not in the heterotetramer alpha(2) beta(2) E2.
the apo-E1 and holo-E1 structures are similar, and the apo-E1 structure is a good model for the E1 component of the PDHc in the absence of the ThDP cofactors.
the absence of ThDP and Mg(2+), as found in the apoenzyme, results in a different hydrogen-bonding network than is found in either the holo-enzyme, or the ThTDP inhibitor complex.
